My experience with Shalimar was nothing but wonderful. 
I wanted to get my engagement ring sized and was told over the phone that it could probably be done within the day. 
When I brought it by, the team confirmed that the jeweler would be able to accommodate my same-day request and that it would be around $40 (simple band, decrease by three full sizes).

The associates' attitudes in dealing with what was a pretty embarrassing situation instantly earned my satisfaction and loyalty as a customer. Very grateful for such a wonderful experience.

Upon arrival, the team confirmed the jeweler could accommodate my request for approximately $40, as it was a simple band needing a reduction of three sizes. I double-checked my size, confirmed it, and left the ring with them.

When I returned that afternoon, the ring was too small. Crucially, Shalimar had sized it perfectly to my initial instruction; the error was mine, as I actually needed a half-size larger. The team was utterly understanding and accommodating. Despite the mistake being my own, they resized the ring again—this time larger—and had it ready for me within an hour at no additional charge.

The associates’ compassionate and professional handling of an embarrassing situation instantly secured my satisfaction and loyalty. I am deeply grateful for such a wonderful and patient customer service experience.

Revise this with your best effort:

input:
I was really between 3 and 4 stars for this one. I LOVE the 96th street Naked Tchopstix so I was very excited to see this one which is closer to my house.
The vibe is totally different as this is geared more to take out although they do have a decent size dining area. You order at the counter and they deliver it.
My daughter and I tried the sushi bowl. You pick up a piece of paper and  select from a choice of proteins, vegetables, rice and toppings. I like the fact that it is on paper and you don't have to guess what things are or have to shout over the counter to tell the server what you want. The sushi bowl was good but not wonderful. The choices particularly of the vegetables seemed a little too limiting and I felt I had more rice than other food items. The sauces were tasty. My husband ordered the Maui roll which is my favorite roll at the 96th street location and this just was not up that standard. It was good but the quality and consistently was not as good as at 96th street. I would go back though and I think a lot of people would be happy with the sushi bowls. I do want to make a comment about the low reviews that people have given the place because of service. People - it is a sushi place - it isn't McDonalds- so it will be a bit slower. You are not going to order and get out of there in five minutes even though it is called express. As a healthy alternative to fast food in the area, it is worth the wait. Oh and try the bubble tea. I had the strawberry and it was quite yummy. Next time I am going to try the vanilla chai.
Revise this with your best effort:
I debated between three and four stars for this location. As a fan of the 96th Street Naked Tchopstix, I was eager to try this branch, which is more convenient for me.

The vibe here is completely different, geared more toward takeout, though there is a reasonably sized dining area. Service is counter-order, with delivery to your table. My daughter and I tried the build-your-own sushi bowl. You mark your selections on a paper menu, choosing from proteins, vegetables, rice, and toppings. I appreciated this system—it’s clear, quiet, and eliminates guessing or shouting your order.

The sushi bowl was good, though not exceptional. The vegetable choices felt somewhat limited, and my bowl seemed disproportionately heavy on rice. The sauces, however, were quite tasty. My husband ordered the Maui roll, a favorite of mine at the 96th Street location, and it didn’t quite meet that standard. It was still good, but the quality and consistency weren’t the same.

I would return, and I believe many would be satisfied with the sushi bowls. I also want to address the low reviews criticizing service speed. Patience is key—this is a sushi spot, not fast food. Even with “Express” in the name, don’t expect to be in and out in five minutes. As a healthier alternative in the area, it’s worth the wait.

Finally, don’t skip the bubble tea. The strawberry was delicious, and I look forward to trying the vanilla chai next time.

The roomy main area had a king bed with night stands, closet, TV, mini fridge, dresser with two drawers, a safe, table for computer or writing, complimentary bottles of water, and three nicely upholstered chairs and table.  The thermostat did a good job controlling the temperature and keeping it comfortable.  Staff were all courteous and helpful.  A very nice place and we enjoyed our stay.
Revise this with your best effort:
We arrived at 2:30 p.m. for a swift and effortless check-in, which included the welcome perk of complimentary valet parking. The Peppermill’s vast scale immediately brought Caesars Palace in Las Vegas to mind. The resort boasts roughly eight on-site restaurants, covering nearly every culinary craving. Its casino floor is equally expansive, rivaling the largest in Vegas. One notable observation: numerous slots were labeled as penny machines, yet upon playing, we discovered minimum bets ranged from 30 cents to $5—a clear case of misleading advertising.

Our room was located on the 12th floor of the Tuscany Tower, offering a pleasant overlook of the extensive pool area. The spacious accommodation included free WiFi, a generous bathroom with dual sinks, ample counter space, a large shower featuring two showerheads, a jetted tub, and even a phone beside the commode. Plentiful towels were provided. The main room held a king bed with nightstands, a closet, a TV, a mini fridge, a two-drawer dresser, a safe, a work table, complimentary water, and three well-upholstered chairs with a table. The thermostat maintained a consistently comfortable temperature.

input:
The only reason I didn't give this restaurant a 5 star rating, is because of one single pretentious waiter. As a 4 night guest at Hotel Palomar, the location of the restaurant is an obvious plus. The first night of my stay, I met a coworker in the restaurant for a cocktail. When we arrived, the host staff were busy and not available, so we just walked in. The restaurant was not too busy, so we just looked at a small table next to the bar and proceeded to take a seat. A waiter came by and I quickly asked if we could have a seat, before sitting down and told him we'd only be having cocktails. He stumbled on his reply, and in an irritated/in-convinced tone, told me "I guess it would be fine" and basically just kept walking mid sentence. My guest and I brushed it off, and started having a conversation while looking at the drink menu. To make a long story short, he was distant and we both got the "couldn't be bothered" vibe from him. When it came to the bill, we asked if it could be split due to company transaction policies, and you would have thought asked him for some inconceivable task. We basically spent the rest of our night and elevator ride to our room in shock of the rudeness we had just experienced. 

Although that situation left a bad taste in our mouth, and the night before we decided to avoid the restaurant, we decided to grab another cocktail and give this place one more try. After looking around and ensuring "last nights waiter" wasn't on shift, we walked over to the bar and started looking over the menu. Instantly, the bartender greeted us with pleasant small talk and made us feel 100% welcome. He asked about our day, recommended cocktails and was a completely genuine person. This guy (I think his name was Ben) is an absolute star! He gave us lessons on Whiskey, described how to make classic cocktails, and was 100% invested in our experience. This is exactly what a bartender at a 4/5 star establishment should be - actually he exceeds that. He was kind, funny, friendly and completely redeemed this restaurant/bar from our terrible experience the night before. 
I also ordered room service last night from this restaurant, and it was amazing. The bacon wrapped dates and chocolate cake are to die for! Great restaurant and amazing bartender(s). Too bad one bad egg could have spoiled this experience.
Revise this with your best effort:
My sole reason for withholding a fifth star is a single, pretentious waiter. As a guest at Hotel Palomar for four nights, the restaurant’s location was a major convenience. On my first evening, I met a coworker there for a cocktail. The host stand was unattended, so we entered and, seeing the space wasn’t busy, approached a small table near the bar. Before sitting, I flagged a passing waiter to ask if it was acceptable, explaining we only wanted drinks. He stumbled over his reply, said in a distinctly irritated and unconvinced tone, “I guess it would be fine,” and then walked away mid-sentence. We brushed it off, but his distant, dismissive “couldn’t-be-bothered” vibe was palpable. When we later asked to split the bill—a standard request due to company policy—he reacted as if we’d asked for something inconceivable. We spent the rest of the night, and the elevator ride up, stunned by such outright rudeness.

That encounter left a sour taste, and we avoided the spot the next night. On our third evening, however, we decided to give it one more try. After confirming that particular waiter wasn’t on shift, we cautiously approached the bar. The contrast was immediate. The bartender—I believe his name was Ben—greeted us with warm small talk, making us feel completely welcome. He asked about our day, offered superb cocktail recommendations, and was utterly genuine. Ben is an absolute star. He gave us a mini-lesson on whiskey, explained how classic cocktails are crafted, and was fully invested in our experience. This is precisely what a bartender at a fine establishment should be—indeed, he exceeds that standard. His kindness, humor, and friendliness completely redeemed the restaurant and bar from our prior terrible experience.

I should also note that I ordered room service from the restaurant last night, and it was exceptional. The bacon-wrapped dates and the chocolate cake are to die for. Ultimately, this is a great restaurant with an amazing bartending team. It’s just a shame that one bad egg nearly spoiled the entire experience.

When asked what we would like to drink I asked for a coke and she brought out a bottle which I stated I wanted the fountain drink.  She said "oh that's only Pepsi".  Never mentioned that they only had bottle drinks for coke.  
We ordered our food which was reasonably priced, asked for sour cream and also to put cheese on the taco.  She let us know cheese was extra.  
It was $2.50 extra for another basket of chips.  
When I received the bill we paid more for the condiments then the actual food.  Side of sour cream 2.00, pico de gallo 2.50, salsa 2.00, chips 2.50, cheese 1.00 and the bottled coke that we didn't want 5.00.  
Just a suggestion...when you order anything make sure to ask if there is an extra charge.
Revise this with your best effort:
This is a good spot if you prefer to pay for each item individually. The food was acceptable, though not memorable.

I politely requested something spicier than the initial tomato sauce, and the server happily brought a better salsa and some pico de gallo. When I ordered a Coke, she brought a bottle. I clarified I wanted a fountain drink, to which she replied, “Oh, that’s only Pepsi.” She hadn’t mentioned bottles were the only option for Coke.

We ordered reasonably-priced food, asking for sour cream and cheese on a taco. We were informed the cheese was extra. An additional basket of chips was $2.50.

The final bill revealed we paid more for condiments than the main dishes: sour cream ($2.00), pico de gallo ($2.50), salsa ($2.00), chips ($2.50), cheese ($1.00), and the unwanted bottled Coke ($5.00).

My suggestion: always ask if there’s an extra charge for *anything* you order.

Overall, Jasmine Rice offers solid, quality Thai food. We’ll definitely return.

input:
We were a bit weary about trying the Shellfish Company on the Wharf as more often than not, many places like these (see Cannery Row, Monterey) feast on a captive audience and provide sub-standard fare at high prices.

However, emboldened by the perennial good reviews on Yelp, we suppressed our initial observations and went ahead with the trying it out. The place is small, so definitely plan ahead. You will have to wait, so either you know, just do so, or perhaps try to visit outside of peak hours. Luckily, our wait was only about 20 minutes as the dinner rush was just leveling off.

The special was the local rock crab - $25 for 3 lbs of California Rock Crab, salad, and your choice of soup/chowder. After taking a look at a few trays of rock crab being served out, the wife and I both opted for it, as it looked awesome.  

The salad/chowder combo was great as you actually received hearty portions of each, so it was a good start. As much as I liked the chowder however, the Shrimp Bisque the wife ordered was amazing, so I would recommend that going forward. 

But enough of prattling on about side dishes: the rock crab tasted just as glorious as it looked. Juicy, buttery chunks of white crab meat await you, just a few cracks away. While the rock crab shells are pretty thick, once cracked, they splinter and separate easily, a good sign they are cooked to perfection. The rock crabs provided a great amount of meat for what I felt to be the least amount of work you're going to do for crab, King or otherwise. 

We were thoroughly satisfied with our meal and along with the special being an overall great value, devouring the Rock Crab at SBSC turned out to be one of the favorite meals on the trip. I think ordering crab here is a safe proposition indeed.
Revise this with your best effort:
We were initially wary of trying the Shellfish Company on the Wharf, as venues in such tourist-centric locations (Cannery Row comes to mind) often serve mediocre food at inflated prices to a captive audience.

Nevertheless, encouraged by consistently strong Yelp reviews, we set aside our skepticism and decided to give it a try. The restaurant is quite small, so planning ahead is essential. Be prepared to wait—either accept that fact or aim for off-peak hours. Fortunately, our wait was only about 20 minutes, as the dinner crowd was beginning to thin.

The evening’s special was local rock crab: $25 for three pounds of California Rock Crab, a salad, and a choice of soup or chowder. After seeing several impressive-looking trays delivered to other tables, my wife and I both chose the special.

The meal began well with the salad and chowder—both portions were substantial and satisfying. While the chowder was quite good, my wife’s Shrimp Bisque was exceptional; I’d recommend opting for that.

But let’s move past the sides: the rock crab was every bit as glorious as it appeared. Behind a few easy cracks lay juicy, buttery chunks of white meat. Though the shells are thick, they splintered cleanly when broken—a sure sign of perfect preparation. These crabs yielded a remarkable amount of meat for what felt like very little effort, especially compared to tackling larger varieties like king crab.

We left thoroughly satisfied. Between the exceptional quality and the outstanding value of the special, our rock crab feast at SBSC ranked among the favorite meals of our trip. Ordering crab here isn’t just a good choice—it’s a reliably excellent one.

input: I LOVE Weaver's Way and really disagree with some of the content in previous reviews. WW is not necessarily meant for convenience shopping. I am a single woman and I find that I have no trouble shopping at the co-op, during peak times or otherwise. I actually find the co-op to be a great place to shop if you live alone because I can get smaller quantities of items than if I shop at the corporate stores like Acme. I also enjoy the work hours - I've worked throughout the store, but most recently, I have been getting in my hours by participating in the membership committee. I wouldn't say that the community is necessarily made up of "tree huggers" and "earth children", though. The community is made up of a variety of similarly-minded folks from different backgrounds. I enjoy having a place to go to where I can obtain locally grown produce, a place that offers more natural, wholesome, and preservative-free foods than chain stores with prices way below that of Whole Foods. I enjoy interacting with other members and contributing to my local and global community. I don't find the membership fee or the work hours to be prohibitive being a single person vs. a family. I don't think that membership in a co-op is for everyone and, if you aren't single, it's definitely not a solo decision. If you're keen on being committed to the Weaver Way values, you couldn't find a better place to shop. If not, stick to the chain stores or just pay the 10% visitors' fee to pop in once in a while.
Revise this with your best effort:
I am a devoted fan of Weaver’s Way and feel compelled to offer a different perspective from some of the earlier reviews. The co-op isn’t designed primarily for convenience, and that’s part of its appeal. As a single person, I shop there easily, even during busy times. In fact, living alone makes it an ideal choice—I can purchase smaller, more manageable quantities than at corporate chains like Acme, which helps me reduce waste.

I also appreciate the member work requirement. I’ve worked in various roles throughout the store and currently serve on the membership committee, which I find rewarding. While some might stereotype the community, it’s not just “tree huggers” or “earth children.” It’s a diverse group of like-minded individuals from all walks of life who value wholesome food and local connection.

What I treasure most is access to locally grown produce and more natural, preservative-free foods—all at prices well below those of Whole Foods. The sense of contributing to my local and global community through everyday shopping is meaningful. Neither the membership fee nor the work hours feel prohibitive, even on a single income.

That said, a co-op isn’t for everyone. If you have a family, joining is a shared decision, not a solo one. But if you genuinely support Weaver’s Way’s values, there’s no better place to shop. If your commitment isn’t there, you can always stick to chain stores or visit occasionally and pay the 10% non-member fee.

input:
After living in the STL area for way over 10 years now, I am both ashamed and remorseful to admit that I ate here for the FIRST time just a few weeks ago. I am ashamed because it's a St. Louis tradition and remorseful because I missed out on it for so..many...years! 

This place is amazing. What is not to love! It's a factory where you can get a tour (Friday-Sunday, noon-5pm on the hour), there's a shop, bar, and dining area. They also host many event with live music on the weekends. It's fun to just kind of wander and look around - don't worry, you'll get a chance because there will likely be a wait before you dine. The beer is, of course, amazing. The Hefeweizen is my personal favorite and a great start for anyone who is not a huge beer drinker (like myself). Additionally, the food is homegrown and damn good. I had the pizza (recommendation from my server) and it was really spectacular, though I'm admittedly a pizza connoisseur so I enjoy a good pizza pie more than most probably ;P My date had a bison burger which was also really good. 

More fun info: the service is great! I think they tend to hire more funky and alternative people (like tattoo parlor staff) which I support. The quality is what makes this place stand out along with the emphasis on local food and brewery. 

It is a little on the pricier side but for all the experience you get and the quality, it is worth it. I will go again and again and you probably should, too!
Revise this with your best effort:
Having been a resident of the St. Louis area for well over a decade, I confess with genuine shame and regret that I dined here for the very first time only recently. My shame stems from neglecting a local institution, and my regret from the many years of excellent experience I foolishly missed.

This place is nothing short of amazing. It’s a vibrant, multifaceted destination: part functioning brewery with tours (Friday-Sunday, on the hour from noon to 5pm), part restaurant and bar, and part event space featuring live music on weekends. The atmosphere invites exploration. You’ll likely have time to wander the shop and admire the space, as a wait for a table is common. The beer is, expectedly, superb. My personal favorite is the Hefeweizen—an accessible and delightful choice for those who aren’t avid beer drinkers, myself included.

The commitment to quality is paramount. The food is outstanding, with a strong emphasis on homegrown, local ingredients. Upon my server’s recommendation, I tried the pizza and found it spectacular (though I admit to being a pizza connoisseur). My date’s bison burger was equally impressive. This quality, paired with a wonderfully quirky and alternative staff who provide excellent service, truly makes the establishment stand out.

While the prices lean toward the higher side, the overall experience—from the exceptional food and drink to the unique ambiance—justifies the cost. It’s a complete package that I plan to enjoy again and again. You should, too.

I visited this restaurant 4 times during my 5 days stay. Crazy, right? Here are a list of reasons/pros:

- If you are a party of two, chances are you get seated right away.
- $9 per dozen of oysters which is a really great deal by any standard!
- They have a seafood shop next door that sells boiled and fresh seafood to- go.
- Our server (same) is very friendly and recognized us every single time.

Now I want to talk about the reasons why I only give it 3 stars.

- We tried a bunch of stuff which are all pretty mediocre. Raw oysters are not cleaned well. So if your schedule is flexible, go to Superior Seafood during their happy hours for their 50 cents/oyster - better quality and cheaper. Turtle soup has a strange taste so I definitely prefer Felix's. A portion of my boiled shrimps are always mushy somhow, maybe boiled for too long?...
- The ambient is inviting but not comfortable so we basically just finished our food and go. 
- Clean the bathroom!!

Will probably visit again if we stay in the area next time or simply just pick up some seafood quickly.
Revise this with your best effort:
During my recent five-day trip, I ended up eating at this restaurant four times—a testament to its convenience, if not perfection. The reasons for my frequent visits are clear: its location near our hotel, reliable hours (open 11 a.m. to 10:30 p.m., even on New Year’s Day), and minimal wait for pairs. At $9 per dozen, the oysters are an outstanding deal, and the friendly server recognized us each visit. The attached seafood shop, offering boiled and fresh items to-go, added to the practicality.

Yet, my overall rating remains just three stars. While convenient, the food was consistently mediocre. The raw oysters were often poorly cleaned—for better quality and price, I’d recommend Superior Seafood during happy hour. The turtle soup had an odd flavor, paling next to Felix’s version, and portions of the boiled shrimp were unpleasantly mushy. Though the atmosphere is inviting, it isn’t comfortable enough to linger. Most notably, the bathrooms urgently need attention.

I’d return for the sake of proximity or a quick seafood pickup, but not for a memorable meal.

input: We stayed at The Saint last year for a girl's trip. The lobby is lovely, they have a cool bar and restaurant that you can't help but to "ohh and ahh" over when you walk in. So I set up my laptop ordered some room service and worked for about 4 hours straight. Left out to buy a bottle and get a mani/pedi.  My girl arrives...its about to be some trouble in NOLA... the two of us and no supervision...we pop out for dinner, come back in giggling as usual and we see it...a HUGH flying roach.  I'm freaked out.  I literally walk right out of the room down to the front desk.  I CANNOT!!!! They tell me they're sending a maintenance worker to handle it.  NOT GOOD ENOUGH! If there's one that's bold enough to show itself, he has other cohorts that prefer to live behind the scenes. They give us another room but tell me they can't do more until 8am.  No the room the move us too also has small spiders and other dead small bugs in the corners of the window. The TV doesn't work and one of the lamps doesn't have bulbs in it! COME ON!  At this point its about 3am and I know I'm not staying here past 8:15am. I dont want to sit my purse let alone my luggage in this hotel! I go online to my normal go to hotel, The W and book us there for the rest of the trip! 8am comes and goes no manager comes to our room. I go down and demand to see someone immediately.  This younger gentlemen comes out and apologizes.  I thank him for his apology and politely request ALL of my money back immediately.   He obliged and asked if  I would consider coming back after changes have been made! Bless his heart. NO dear!
Revise this with your best effort:
Our girls’ trip to New Orleans began with such promise at The Saint. The lobby was stunning, and the bar and restaurant elicited immediate “oohs” and “aahs”—the perfect blend of chic ambiance and subtle sophistication I expect from a nice hotel. The staff was wonderfully friendly. Settling in early to tackle some work, I thought, “This is going to be a fantastic weekend.”

After a productive afternoon, I headed out for a manicure and a bottle of wine. Once my friend arrived, we were ready for a classic NOLA adventure. We enjoyed dinner, returned to the hotel giggling, and then saw it: a massive flying roach. I was horrified. I marched straight to the front desk, utterly unable to cope. They promised to send maintenance, but that wasn’t good enough. A bug that bold surely had hidden companions.

We were moved to another room, but the issues only multiplied. Small spiders and dead insects dotted the window corners, the television was broken, and a lamp lacked bulbs. By 3 a.m., I knew we wouldn’t stay past morning. I didn’t even want to set my purse down. I promptly booked us into my reliable standby, The W, for the remainder of the trip.

The promised 8 a.m. manager visit never happened. I went downstairs and insisted on speaking to someone immediately. A young gentleman appeared, offering apologies. I thanked him and politely demanded a full refund, which he processed. He then asked if we might consider returning after improvements were made. Bless his heart. The answer, of course, was a firm and final no.

The Quaker (Chicken version) - Delicious. They make their chicken steaks with the chunky chicken, which I like much more than the shredded version. They could season the chicken more, but the cheese was melted perfectly and the veggies were fresh. 

The fries - crisp and flavorful. I didn't even need ketchup, and I always eat ketchup on my fries

The onion rings - a little greasy, but very tasty and crisp. The onions stayed in the breading and didn't slide out when you bit them (which I hate). 

Spanakopita - mine was a little over cooked, but the flavors were really good

Baklava - VERY GOOD! 

Signature Salad - The veggies they use are very fresh which will make or break a salad. Their balsamic is great too!

The (turkey) Greek Burger - one of the best turkey burgers I've ever had! The patty was moist and flavorful all on its own, but then they top it with what must be homemade tzatziki. I could eat a bowl of that stuff! My burger had romaine instead of the advertised arugula, but it was very fresh, so I didn't mind as much. I also asked for feta, which I didn't get, but that sauce made me forget all about it. 

Overall, this place is great! Provided they don't stray from the high quality standard they are setting, I will keep going back.

I’m giving this spot four stars because they’ve genuinely earned it—though they’re absolutely five-star material once a few kinks are worked out. They’re newly opened, so some of the hiccups I’ve noticed (I work nearby and have visited several times) will likely smooth over time. I will say they’re very willing to make things right when a mistake happens, which counts for a lot.

Where they truly shine is the food, which is REALLY good. Unlike some other reviewers, I’d argue the pizza isn’t their strong suit—it tends to be a bit greasy, and the cheese doesn’t taste like pure mozzarella. But nearly everything else has been excellent:

• **The Quaker (chicken version):** Delicious. They use a chunky, hearty chicken steak instead of shredded chicken. While the chicken could use more seasoning, the cheese was perfectly melted and the veggies were fresh.

• **The fries:** Crisp and so flavorful I didn’t even reach for ketchup—and I always use ketchup.

• **Onion rings:** A touch greasy, but very tasty and crisp. Best of all, the onion stayed put in the breading instead of sliding out when bitten.

• **Spanakopita:** Mine was slightly overdone, but the flavors were spot-on.

• **Baklava:** VERY GOOD.

• **Signature Salad:** Exceptionally fresh veggies (which make or break a salad) and a great balsamic dressing.

• **Greek Burger (turkey):** One of the best turkey burgers I’ve had. The patty was moist and flavorful on its own, topped with what must be homemade tzatziki—I could eat a bowl of that sauce. My burger came with romaine instead of arugula and forgot the feta, but the tzatziki made up for it.

Overall, this place is great. Provided they maintain the high standards they’re setting, I’ll definitely be back.

input:
Went here based on the high ratings and raves from people.  The entire experience was underwhelming from start to finish.  Their website which is fairly useless if you want to figure out the menu before going, you have to pick your location choice out of 3 locations and then drill down to the bottom to see the weak descriptions of their menu offering, no explanations and no price, just this

    Roast Beef
    Roast Beef Combo
    Roast Pork
    Roast Pork Combo
    Baked Ham
    Baked Ham Combo
    Roast Turkey
    Roast Turkey Combo
    Broccoli Rabe
    Broccoli Rabe Combo


No explanation of whats in a combo (its just where they add cheese by the way)

The table placecard (instead of menu) had a more detailed description than the website.  

When I walked in, its more bar than restaurant, no big deal, but there were tables.  Since I couldnt decide and the sandwiches werent too expensive at $6.85, I got the roast beef and roast port combos.

I got my two sandwiches fast enough, but the roast beef was cold and the roast pork was hot.  Not sure how a cook (for lack of a better word) could serve 2 things at the same time with such a temperature differential, one was obviously sitting for awhile.  I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef while I finished the roast pork, and supposedly it was reheated, since it was warmer, but it was still cold-ish compared to my roast pork I had just finished.  The waitress did offer to replace it when she inquired, but I was in a hurry and didnt really care for a hot version of this sandwich.

The sandwiches were very skimpy on meat, but they "made up for it" by adding too much gravy to make it overly messy and the bread was disintegrating.  The menu place card mentions the "wet meat" option where you get less gravy, I strongly recommend you get it that style, especially if the gravy overpower the meat and structural integrity of the sandwich.

Based on the high ratings and enthusiastic reviews, I had high hopes for this place. Unfortunately, the entire experience proved underwhelming.

It began with their website, which is nearly useless for planning. To view a menu, you must first select one of three locations, then scroll to the bottom only to find a bare list with weak descriptions and no prices—just items like “Roast Beef,” “Roast Beef Combo,” and so on. There was no explanation of what a “combo” entails (it simply adds cheese, by the way).

The physical table placard offered slightly more detail than the website. The venue itself felt more like a bar than a restaurant, though tables were available. Since the sandwiches were reasonably priced at $6.85, I decided to try both a roast beef combo and a roast pork combo.

The sandwiches arrived quickly, but immediately there was an issue: the roast beef was cold, while the roast pork was hot. It was puzzling how two items served simultaneously could have such a temperature difference—clearly one had been sitting out. I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef while I ate the pork. It returned warmer, yet still noticeably cooler than the pork had been. She kindly offered a replacement, but I was short on time and had lost my appetite for a hot version.

Both sandwiches were surprisingly skimpy on meat. To compensate, they were drenched in excessive gravy, making them overly messy and causing the bread to disintegrate. The menu does note a “wet meat” option for less gravy; I strongly recommend choosing that style. Otherwise, the gravy overwhelms both the flavor of the meat and the structural integrity of the sandwich itself.

input:
Too big, too expensive and too far from Downtown.  

I was here for a conference, which seemed like an awesome idea. It wasn't.  I'm in Direct Sales and (like most people at this conference) don't have tons of extra money to spend on mediocre meals when I'm traveling.  $10 for a slice of generic pizza, small side salad and a soda for lunch.   I understand it's a hotel but there weren't any options close by.  Just getting your car from valet was a hassle and took a lot of time.  Being such a big property, it made getting to restaurants off the property really time intensive.  Since you're so far out of Nashville (out near the airport), the good little holes you find when you're in a city are pretty nonexistent.  

The property itself was great.  The hotel is HUGE but really pretty.  I enjoyed walking around but was really happy when I found what I didn't know existed...a shortcut between my room and the Convention Center.  It took my 10-15 minute walk down to about 3 minutes!  BONUS!  Like I said, this place is ginormous.  

Room: Our room was great.  I shared a wonderful suite in the Garden Conservatory with 2 other girls.  We were under a group rate and my friend was quoted $200/night, which is awesome for the space we had.  We had a large room (probably used as a hospitality suite for groups) for socializing.  It had a great bar area set-up and a nice big fridge and lots of drawer space.  Our bedroom was separated by doors that could be locked from either side (like an adjoining room), so it looked like the hospitality suite could be reserved without reserving the room.  It was different than what I was expecting, but whatevs.  It was fine.  So, I wasn't there at check-in.  The girl who reserved the room checked in a couple days earlier than my friend and I.  So, Sunday comes, and the bill was waiting for us when we woke up.  Our friend was charged $1200 for one room (I'm guessing the suite) and $1400 for the other room.  YEP.  She reserved what she thought was a 2 room suite for $200.  The bedroom door was closed when she got there and she asked them to open it up. It was all arranged by the bellman.  She was never told that the bedroom wasn't included....kind of necessary if you're staying over for 6 nights, dontcha think???  So, she's being charged $2600 for what was supposed to be $1200.  Last I heard, the Gaylord's legal department was investigating what she was told, what she wasn't told and if they should charge her the entire amount.  

Checkout:  A FREAKING NIGHTMARE.  Between the money situation, which was not resolved as of late this week, and the 45 minute wait for a cart (in a hotel that holds thousands of people, you'd think they'd be plentiful and they aren't) and a 25 minute wait for the car, my friend and I decided to sweat it out and schlep our goods to the door where our car would be delivered to us.  It was not a short walk and we had a TON of stuff, which meant multiple trips.  UGH.

I'm sure I'll be back for another conference (I am pretty sure my company has booked this for at least one more year....) but I'm not going to be happy about it.  I might even consider driving down, staying in a hotel somewhere downtown and driving out to the Conference stuff.
Revise this with your best effort:
Too big, too expensive, and too far from everything.

I attended a conference here, which initially seemed like a great plan. It wasn’t. I work in direct sales and, like most attendees, don’t have a large travel budget for overpriced, mediocre meals. Think $10 for a slice of generic pizza, a small side salad, and a soda. While I understand hotel pricing, the real issue was the lack of alternatives. The property is so isolated near the airport that none of Nashville’s affordable, local gems are within reach. Even getting your car from valet is a time-consuming hassle, and venturing off-site for a meal becomes a major expedition.

The resort itself is undeniably impressive—a massive, beautifully designed complex. I enjoyed exploring it, though its sheer size is daunting. A major victory was discovering an unmarked shortcut that slashed my 10-15 minute trek to the convention center down to three minutes. A true bonus in a place this ginormous.

**The Room:** Our accommodations were great, at first. I shared a lovely suite in the Garden Conservatory with two friends under a group rate. My friend was quoted $200 per night, which was fantastic for the space: a large hospitality-style living area with a bar setup, a big fridge, and plenty of storage. The bedroom was separated by doors that locked from both sides, like an adjoining room. It was different than expected, but fine.

Here’s where it unraveled. I wasn’t present at check-in. The friend who booked arrived first. When my other friend and I arrived on Sunday, the bill was waiting. She was charged $1,200 for one room (the suite) and an additional $1,400 for the other—the bedroom. Yes, she had reserved what she believed was a two-room suite for $200/night. Upon arrival, the bedroom door was locked; a bellman opened it at her request. At no point was she informed the bedroom wasn’t included in her original reservation—a rather crucial detail for a six-night stay. Now, she’s facing a $2,600 charge for what was supposed to cost $1,200. The last update was that Gaylord’s legal department is “investigating” what was or wasn’t communicated.

**Checkout:** An absolute nightmare. With the billing dispute still unresolved and faced with a 45-minute wait for a luggage cart (shockingly scarce for a hotel that holds thousands) and a 25-minute wait for the car, my friend and I gave up. We decided to sweat it out, making multiple exhausting trips to schlep all our conference materials to the front drive. It was a long, frustrating end to the stay.

I’ll likely be back for another conference—my company has probably booked it again—but I won’t be happy. Next time, I’m seriously considering staying at a downtown hotel and commuting out. The inconvenience and expense just aren’t worth it.

I noticed the manager in a green sweater lingering around the entrance and then two cop cars with lights flashing pulled up and 3 officers rushed in walked to the table next to us that the manager was pointing to and one of the officer's proceeded to pull out their handcuffs and tell the guy delivering food to put food down at the table and hands behind his back. They escorted him near the front door and had him sit down for a moment before taking him outside in freeZing cold with no jacket where he stood for a few minutes while cops came in and out of restaurant. 

This entire thing was poorly handled, disturbing and unsettling not only to the customers but the other staff. They should have had the cops walk back away from where customers were and deal with it there. Then all the managers disappeared not available to talk to any of the customers let alone apologize or acknowledge people being unsettled. 

No one needs to know why the arrest happened but there needed to be more care for customers and staff in how it was handled. 

Not ok!!!

I do wish the staff was a little more knowledgable on what they carry but I understand that that's a lot to ask. I also wish that the store was bigger, brighter and cleaner. The cramped aisles, dust bunnies and flickering, yellow fluorescent lights don't exactly give that same "beauty/trendy" feeling that other beauty stores have. If I could give one piece of advice to management it would be to work on the appearance of the store, other than that I'm pretty happy with Sally's.
Revise this with your best effort:
Of all the beauty stores in the area, Sally’s stands out for its unparalleled selection of hair supplies. The staff is consistently friendly and the shelves are well-stocked, making it my go-to for experimenting with new styles. I do wish the employees were slightly more knowledgeable about the products, though I understand that’s a tall order.

My primary suggestion would be to revitalize the store’s appearance. Currently, the cramped aisles, occasional dust, and flickering fluorescent lights detract from the trendy, inviting atmosphere that competitors offer. A brighter, cleaner, and more spacious environment would better reflect the quality products inside. Beyond that, I remain quite satisfied with Sally’s and its vast array of options.

input:
Let me preface by saying that I have been getting my hair cut by a guy in Austin for seven years, even though I've lived in other cities for half that time. He is that good. The couple of times that I've strayed, I have been severely disappointed in the outcome. But I wasn't planning a trip back to Austin for a while and badly needed a cut, so I decided to bite the bullet.

My friend walks in a few weeks ago with *srsly* the cutest short hair cut. And so I ask her who and where, and she says Rodney Mitchell. I figured that this place would be too expensive, but she corrected my thinking on the matter. So I called to make an appointment with her guy (whose name I sadly cannot remember at the moment) and Rodney answered the phone. Turns out the guy my friend had seen didn't do morning appointments and all my afternoons were filled, so Rodney said "look, I'm the owner, I can absolutely vouch for Allison who has several openings in the next few days." So I thought, alright, he's the owner so he knows his stuff--I'll do it.

Allison absolutely did not disappoint. First off, she's a total sweetheart, but not super chatty (I appreciate stylists who can be content to both hold and not hold a convo while working) so there was no pressure there. I came in with my laptop and several photos I'd found that approximated what I wanted in a haircut, as I couldn't find exactly the right one. We talked about it a bit, discussed front and back length, bangs, etc. and she said alright and went to it. What she gave me was the cutest damn shaggy bob that I never thought possible. I seriously can't wait to go back.

One of the other awesome things about RMS is that they give you a discount for your first visit and I believe they have some kind of discount for students and teachers. They also will give you *another* discount when you refer people. So I got my friend a discount, and then referred a friend, so I'll get another discount when I go back for my next cut. All good things when you're trying your best to be a frugal  grad student.
Revise this with your best effort:
For seven years, I’ve had the same hairstylist in Austin. I’ve even flown back to see him while living in other cities, because he’s that good. Every time I’ve tried someone else, I’ve been disappointed. Recently, however, a trip to Austin wasn’t feasible and I desperately needed a cut, so I decided to bite the bullet and try a new place locally.

The decision was made when my friend walked in with the *cutest* short haircut. She referred me to Rodney Mitchell Salon. I initially assumed it would be too expensive, but she assured me it wasn’t. When I called to book with her specific stylist, Rodney himself answered. Unfortunately, that stylist had no morning availability, and my afternoons were packed. Rodney then said, “I’m the owner, and I can absolutely vouch for Allison. She has several openings soon.” His confidence as the owner convinced me to give Allison a try.

Allison did not disappoint. She is a total sweetheart and, importantly, not overly chatty—I appreciate a stylist who is comfortable with both conversation and quiet focus. I arrived prepared, with my laptop and multiple photos that *approximated* my desired look, since I couldn’t find one perfect example. We consulted on the length, bangs, and shape. Then she got to work. The result was the most perfect, shaggy bob—a cut I never thought would suit me so well. I am genuinely thrilled and can’t wait to return.

A final, fantastic perk about Rodney Mitchell Salon is their discount structure. They offer a first-time client discount, and I believe they also have one for students and teachers. Additionally, they provide a referral discount. So, I secured a discount for my friend who referred me, and I’ve already referred another friend, which will give me a discount on my next visit. These savings are a major bonus when you’re navigating life as a frugal graduate student.

input:
So much to like about this place--the beautiful Mercer Building location, the spaciousness, the lovely, friendly baristas. But there are a couple of important cons for me. Biggest being, the music is constant and too loud, ruining everything you go to a coffee shop to do: read, work, reflect, or enjoy a good conversation. When I asked for it to be turned down, they told me they can't--it just plays at one level all the time, and the speakers  are everywhere so you can't get away from it. It sucks.

Secondly, if you're a tea drinker, you're out of luck. They don't serve the tea in pots, but huge, sloppy individual filters--it makes your beverage totally ungainly, hard to drink and is really off putting.

Pros: gluten free goodies and yummy Italian sodas. I'd love to spend more time here, but the music usually drives me out after 10 minutes.
Revise this with your best effort:
There is much to admire here: the lovely Mercer Building setting, the spacious interior, and the genuinely friendly baristas. However, two significant drawbacks affect my experience.

Primarily, the relentlessly loud music undermines the very purpose of a café. It hinders reading, working, quiet reflection, or conversation. Upon request, I was informed the volume is fixed and the pervasive speakers offer no escape. It’s a major disruption.

Secondly, tea drinkers are poorly served. Instead of a pot, tea arrives in an oversized, sloppy individual filter, making the beverage awkward and unappealing to drink.

Notable positives include delicious gluten-free pastries and Italian sodas. While I wish I could stay longer, the oppressive music typically drives me out within ten minutes.

(Word count: 150)

input:
Spice n Grill has the best Indian food in St. Louis. We had the beef nihari, palak paneer, and naan. The palak and beef were perfectly spiced, adequately spicy, and crave-worthy. I've never had a nihari dish before and I will be sure to try it again. 

The restaurant doesn't have great seating  in the store, so I will take food to go next time. The owner served us and he was very nice, but I don't think people eat in the restaurant very often. 

I was so excited to see that the previous owners of 'Indian Food' have opened a new restaurant and I would recommend it if you're in the mood for delicious take-out.
Revise this with your best effort:
Spice n Grill serves the best Indian food in St. Louis. We tried the beef nihari, palak paneer, and naan. Both the palak and beef were perfectly spiced, with a crave-worthy heat. The nihari was a first for me, and I’ll definitely order it again.

The in-store seating is limited, making it ideal for takeout. The owner was very kind, but the space seems geared more toward to-go orders. I was thrilled to learn this is the new venture from the former owners of ‘Indian Food.’ I highly recommend it for anyone seeking delicious take-out.

(Word count: 104)

input:
I've come from Cali where boba is very common there. However I was thinking this place would have had the same feel. After being told this place branched off from California, I was disappointed. 

I'm more of a natural person. I enjoy real flavor, real fruits, and of course the perfect boba. I notice that some flavors were used by real fruits but others were just powder which I could definitely taste the different. Especially the taro flavor, being one of my favorites. 

But, if you're not too concern about natural vs powder flavor then this place could be good for you. They ask what level you would like you sweetness and any additional add-ons you would like. I always get boba but sometimes the grass jelly is pretty good too! I'd recommend you try. 

This is also a good place to catch up, talk, play board, card games and even do homework. I know it's always busy with students from the U of A and being told from them it's a nice area to just hang out, that's a pretty good sign. 

Maybe I'm just too picky, but I think it could be better. 

"See it, taste it, Yelp it"
Revise this with your best effort:
Coming from California, where boba is a staple, I expected a similar experience here—especially after learning this spot branched off from a West Coast original. Unfortunately, it fell short.

I prefer natural flavors, real fruit, and perfectly chewy boba. While some drinks here use genuine ingredients, others rely on powdered mixes. The difference is noticeable, particularly in the taro, which is usually a favorite of mine.

If you’re less particular about natural versus artificial flavoring, you might enjoy it. They let you customize sweetness and add-ons like boba or grass jelly—the latter is quite good. It’s a lively space, popular with University of Arizona students for hanging out, playing games, or studying.

Maybe I’m just picky, but I believe it could be better.

"See it, taste it, Yelp it."

input:

input:
Underrated burger alert!!

Randomly came into Pag's during a stroll around Doylestown. The menu wasn't super appealing, actually, so I just went with a cheeseburger. Legitimately, one of the best cheeseburgers I've had in a while! Tasted like a quality Big Mac! Patty wasn't too thick, bun didn't overshadow the burger and whatever sauce they used - YUM.

We were in the wine bar section - ambiance is really nice; def not very kid friendly (we had our son with us.) but staff was friendly and accommodating.

We will totally be back next time we are in the mood for a good burger!
Revise this with your best effort:
Don’t sleep on this burger!

I wandered into Pag’s in Doylestown on a whim. The menu didn’t wow me, so I simply ordered a cheeseburger. It was legitimately one of the best I’ve had in ages—reminiscent of a premium Big Mac! The patty was perfectly proportioned, the bun didn’t overwhelm, and the special sauce was delicious.

We sat in the wine bar: a nice, adult-oriented ambiance (note: not very kid-friendly, though the staff was wonderfully accommodating with our son).

We’ll absolutely return whenever a burger craving strikes.

input: Absolutely wonderful food & service! Go there for lunch/dinner with my boyfriend at least once every two weeks. Prices are very much reasonable. input: Pretty slow service and the waitresses aren't very kind. I guess I was expecting something different at a diner with high ratings but I understand it's in the middle of a tourist area. However, service should be a priority. Something that really bothered me was how much trash was left on the floor of the outside deck- it all has the potential to blow right into the ocean. NOT OKAY. I had to stand up several times to grab straw wrappers and napkins before they blew into the water. If you're going to have a waterfront/beach front business, be responsible about it. It would be a very easy fix-just a screen on the bottom of the fence. The food was good but I won't be back.
Revise this with your best effort:
The service was disappointingly slow, and the staff was less than welcoming. For a highly-rated diner, I expected better—though its tourist location may be a factor. Regardless, service should remain a priority. What truly upset me was the amount of trash littering the outdoor deck, poised to blow into the ocean. I repeatedly had to catch straw wrappers and napkins to prevent them from reaching the water. Operating a waterfront business demands responsibility. A simple fix, like a screen along the fence bottom, would help immensely. While the food was good, the overall experience means I won’t be returning.

input: It's no different than any other Chinese place. Same menu, etc. this place does have some good lunch specials though, and the food is always ready when I go to pick it up.

input:
You think Value City, you think cheap value, right? Wrong! 

Think Rothman prices with Ashley Furniture pieces. Not a Broyhill in sight. 

Negatives:
- Entertainment centers and TV stand selection is small, and over priced selection.
-Their "Clearance" section is laughable and not much of a sale. No one is going to pay $299 for a nicked up coffee table that was originally $350. Go lower. 
- Sectionals by themselves average around $1,000 by brands I've never heard of. 
- The staff hangs out like a clique chatting in the middle of the store rather than helping customers. 
-Dining sets are nothing special and overpriced as well. I've seen the same selection everywhere else at a lower price. 
-5% military discount? Ooooh you're going to knock $20 off my sofa! 

Only Positive:
-They have a few modern pieces. 

Overall:

I think they're high for low quality-mediocre furniture. Shop around town. Or if you do find something you must have here, wait for a holiday sale.
Revise this with your best effort:
You might assume Value City Furniture means affordable value, but think again. The reality feels more like Rothman’s pricing for Ashley Furniture–level pieces, with no premium brands like Broyhill in sight.

The drawbacks are significant. The selection of entertainment centers and TV stands is limited and overpriced. Their "Clearance" section is a poor joke—offering minimal savings, like a nicked $350 coffee table marked down to $299. Sectionals from unknown brands average around $1,000. Dining sets are unremarkable and priced higher than competitors. The 5% military discount is paltry, barely making a dent. Furthermore, staff often congregate and chat instead of assisting customers.

On the plus side, they do carry a few modern pieces.

Overall, the store offers low to mediocre quality at inflated prices. I recommend shopping around first. If you must buy something here, wait for a major holiday sale.

input: I really like Franzone's. The owner is typically around, super friendly, and seems to really care about the product. input:
Finally had the chance to stop by Bab Cafe...what took us so long!  Both of us being Asian food fanatics, we are so happy to have Bab Cafe part of our ever expanding culinary experience here in Reno.

With the guidance of the very friendly and knowledgeable staff, we quickly got a hang of what to order, though there will be many more choices on our future visits. The sauce bar gives you the opportunity to mix things up and the included miso soup is a definite bonus.  Great value for such a fresh, enjoyable meal.  Convenient downtown location to take away, dine in or have it delivered via UberEats.
Revise this with your best effort:
Finally made it to Bab Cafe—why did we wait so long? As avid fans of Asian cuisine, we’re thrilled to add this spot to our growing list of Reno favorites.

The friendly, knowledgeable staff helped us choose, though we’ll need many return trips to try everything. We both opted for the Jeyuk Top-Bab (spicy pork)—what incredible flavor! input:
Ichicoro Ane gets lots of things right and the best part about it is the combination of the ambiance with the food choices and whiskey selection. I'm very happy with this location and the servers I have encountered so far have been helpful and pleasant.

The katsu is great and I highly recommend it to people looking for a more filling dish on the menu. The bao buns were also good for a lighter fish. I haven't had anything I really regretted trying, but definitely ask your server about the portion sizes of each dish since they vary across the menu.

The cocktail selection is excellent. I even had a special Japanese Old Fashioned last time which was a little expensive, but well worth it for some quality Japanese whiskey. 

I'm looking forward to exploring the menu little by little. The best way to experience this is in a group setting so you can try more things and it really reminds me of Izakayas or Japanese pubs I visited in Japan and Korea.
Revise this with your best effort:
Ichicoro Ane excels by masterfully pairing its ambiance with an outstanding food menu and whiskey selection. I’ve been consistently pleased with this location, and the servers have always been both helpful and pleasant.

For a hearty option, the katsu is excellent and highly recommended. The bao buns are a perfect lighter choice. While I’ve enjoyed everything I’ve tried, it’s wise to ask about portion sizes, as they vary significantly across the menu.

The cocktails are superb. I recently tried a special Japanese Old Fashioned; though slightly pricey, it was well worth it for the quality of whiskey.

I look forward to gradually exploring more dishes. This spot is best enjoyed in a group, where you can sample widely—the shared, lively atmosphere truly evokes the authentic Izakayas I visited in Japan and Korea.

input: Love this bakery!! Great breakfast sandwiches, coffee, and donuts! My friend and I love coming on weekend mornings

input: There is a great selection of whiskey/bourbon to suit anyone's taste. We had burgers with the fried egg on it and it was soo good and probably one of the best burgers I've ever had. input: A++ for ambience. Very cozy English pub feel. Great drinks too - the bartenders here know how to mix 'em. That being said, the prices are steep (I paid $7 for a standard mixed drink) and the seating is limited.

input: Very cozy place to have a drink with friends.  The drinks were tasty and were served in very pretty glasses reminiscent of those some of our grandmothers had in their china cabinets. On the downside, all of the drinks seemed to have some combination of ginger, lime, and honey with the main difference being the kind of liquor you wanted in your drink.  So the choices felt limited.  I ordered the bacon wrapped dates, and have to admit that I was choking them down because I was hungry.  They tasted like they were double dipped in sugar.  Also, once another 10 or so people came in, it was very hard to hear each other because the noise level skyrocketed, which is surprising with so much fabric in the room.  The servers were nice and left us alone except to check on us every so often.  I don't recall being offered a second drink when my glass was taken away.
Revise this with your best effort: This cozy spot is ideal for a casual drink among friends. The cocktails were delicious, served in charming vintage glassware that evoked a sense of nostalgia. However, the menu felt repetitive, as nearly every drink was a variation on ginger, lime, and honey, differentiated only by the base spirit. For food, the bacon-wrapped dates were overly sweet, as if candied, making them a challenge to finish. While the servers were pleasant and unobtrusive, the acoustics were a letdown. Once the space filled with about ten more patrons, the noise level soared, making conversation difficult despite the fabric-draped interior. A minor service lapse occurred when my empty glass was cleared without an offer for another round.

input:

I should have gone for, and I will recommend others in the future to find another rental company such as Hertz, at which you can always find codes to waive this crazy fee.

Not about this location but where I returned my car.

"Return Location Address and Phone Number :
PORT JEFFERSON STATION
320 ROUTE 112
PORT JEFFERSON STATION, NY 11776-1010
Tel.: (631) 474-2100"

This address is totally WRONG!!! I kept asking people around this address for the right location and wasted another hour when returning my car!

I believe this location is critically understaffed. Customers are perpetually waiting; it took over an hour simply to get my rental car ready. Matters worsened the next morning when, just before a family trip, I discovered the windshield washer reservoir was completely empty. I was forced to return, wasting another hour as they refilled it.

My rental began on May 18th, very close to my 25th birthday on June 6th, yet I was still charged an exorbitant underage fee—$20 per day before tax—with no possibility of a waiver. input:
We used The Hollander Hotel for our wedding hotel and it was an absolutely incredible experience.  I will never get tired of raving about our experience.  We were honored to use the Hollander not only for our room block and wedding night suite, but we also used the Tap Room as our after-party location and we hosted a brunch for our guests on the beautiful patio on Sunday morning after the wedding.  Everything was perfection and if we could do it all over again, we wouldn't change a thing!

The hotel property is absolutely charming.  The décor in the lobby is beautiful, eclectic, and very welcoming.  The Tap Room is a great place for people to gather with intimate booths and large tables for bigger parties.  The Bar has an amazing selection of local and craft beers and the servers and bartenders are all professional and fast! We were able to use the Lobby and Tap Room for some of our wedding photographs too, and they all look wonderful!

The rooms are very pleasant and quaint and our guests all complimented on how clean and cozy they were.  The prices were also wonderful and our guests were able to enjoy downtown St. Pete because of the great location.  The shuttle is also very convenient and a great experience for guests!

The brunch was perfect.  Not only was the price great for an all-you-can-enjoy feast, but the food is delicious and homemade.  The wonderful gentleman who makes the omelets is friendly, fast, and takes great pride in his work.  He is also a talented baker and I couldn't get enough of the chocolate muffins he made!  The service at the new coffee/dessert café was wonderful!  The Patio was a great place to visit with our guests and enjoy the beautiful St. Pete weather. We look forward to many more brunches there in the future! 

Finally, the best part of all is the management and team at the Hollander.  Nick and Will treated us like their own family.  They went above and beyond to ensure that each of our guests felt like they were at home and comfortable.  Zach at the front desk was so friendly and patient with me as I called checking on our room block.  The entire team was just a delight and so very accommodating.  They take great pride in ensuring that every guest has a wonderful experience.  We just adore everyone there!  I absolutely loved working with them and would recommend this beautiful hotel to anyone!
Revise this with your best effort:
Our wedding experience at The Hollander Hotel was nothing short of incredible, and we will never tire of singing its praises. We were honored to utilize the hotel in multiple ways: for our guest room block, our wedding night suite, our after-party in the Tap Room, and a farewell brunch on the beautiful patio the following morning. Every detail was perfection; if we could relive it, we wouldn’t change a single thing.

The property itself is utterly charming. The lobby décor is a beautiful, eclectic, and welcoming mix. The Tap Room proved an ideal gathering spot, offering intimate booths and large tables for groups, complemented by an amazing selection of local and craft beers. The bartenders and servers were consistently professional and efficient. We even incorporated the lobby and Tap Room into our wedding photographs, with stunning results.

Guest accommodations were pleasant and quaint, with many of our attendees complimenting the clean, cozy rooms. The pricing was wonderful, and the prime location allowed everyone to easily enjoy downtown St. Petersburg. The provided shuttle service was also a convenient and appreciated amenity.

Our Sunday brunch was flawless. The value for an all-you-can-enjoy feast was outstanding, and the food was deliciously homemade. The omelet station was manned by a wonderfully friendly and fast gentleman who took clear pride in his work—a talented baker, his chocolate muffins were irresistible! Service at the new coffee and dessert café was equally excellent. The patio offered the perfect setting to visit with guests and savor the lovely St. Pete weather. We eagerly anticipate returning for many future brunches.

Above all, the true highlight was the management and team. Nick and Will treated us like family, going above and beyond to ensure every guest felt at home and comfortable. Zach at the front desk was exceptionally friendly and patient with my numerous calls about the room block. The entire staff was a delight—accommodating, proud of their work, and dedicated to creating wonderful experiences. We absolutely adore everyone there. It was a pleasure to work with them, and we wholeheartedly recommend this beautiful hotel to anyone.

input:
Although there are countless little Mexican places below Washington Avenue, I never get sick of them and always look forward to trying the new kid on the block. This time it was El Sabor Poblano on Federal, which could not look less special if it tried.

I liked that there were 3 fish tacos on the menu.  I picked the fried and battered version, though the tortilla chip covered fish could have been awesome. I was instantly impressed when I opened one of my three and found that El Sabor puts an entire filet of fish in each taco! The flakey meat had no fishy taste. These tacos came with the more American toppings of lettuce and, tomato, and cheese. I bet I could have gotten cilantro and onion if I asked. The sole staff member in the place seemed happy to accommodate us- well, we were the only ones dining in.

Another taco filling option that comes with more traditional toppings is the super crispy chorizo, only $8 for 3. There was no detectable gristle here, something I have often come across at this little places.

As unassuming as it looks, this particular South Philly Mexican place is worth stopping by.
Revise this with your best effort:
While countless small Mexican spots line the streets below Washington Avenue, I never tire of them and am always eager to try the newest arrival. My latest visit was to El Sabor Poblano on Federal—a place that could not look more unassuming if it tried.

I was pleased to see three fish taco options. I chose the fried and battered version, though the tortilla-chip-crusted alternative also sounded tempting. Upon opening one of my three tacos, I was instantly impressed: each contained an entire filet. The flaky meat had no fishy taste, and it was topped with more American-style accompaniments: lettuce, tomato, and cheese. I suspect cilantro and onion were available upon request. The sole staff member was happy to accommodate us—though, to be fair, we were the only diners.

Another standout is the super-crispy chorizo taco, served with traditional toppings and just $8 for three. Notably, there was no detectable gristle—a common pitfall at such modest establishments.

Despite its plain appearance, this particular South Philly Mexican spot is well worth a stop.

input:

The manager was nice enough to offer to fill cups of coffee for us while we waited. But I thought it was odd that they just didn't refill the pot for everyone who was waiting. 

Now for the food...They have these 1/2 and 1/2 combos. Which I love! I got a turkey Reuben and salad. I asked for lots of sauerkraut, and they charged $0.50 for it.. Which is no biggie but I'd expect a lot of kraut. Sadly there was not a lot of it.. But it was still a delicious sandwhich.  :) My friend got the sunrise chile rellenos. input:
Thank you for a lovely morning!  I was in NJ early and decided to stop in for a delicious diner breakfast.  I got a taylor ham, egg, and cheese and a short stack of blueberry pancakes (I simply couldn't decide between sweet or savory, plus leftovers are never a bad thing).  

The egg sandwich was fantastic.  I was nervous when they said they didn't have kaiser rolls so I went with a hamburger roll.  It was an excellent decision.  The roll was excellent - not just an average cheap hamburger roll.  They layered the cheese on the sandwich, which to me is a must for a true egg sandwich.  It was served with home fries, which were sauteed with large slices of peppers and onions.  I'm not the biggest breakfast potatoes fan, but these were great and I appreciated that they didn't clearly just scoop some food from a huge pile of pre-cooked home fries.

The pancakes were great and fluffy.  My one gripe was their use of smuckers pre-packaged syrup.  I realize that if they put syrup in a container, it probably wouldn't be real maple syrup, but I sort of wish I didn't know that they were giving me sub-par syrup.

The server was friendly and very attentive.  The coffee refills were constant, and the coffee was actually good (so many diners fail at coffee).  Bonus points for the server agreeing not to judge my decision to get two breakfasts.

All around, I loved this place and hope to go back soon.  Long live the Jersey diners!

Faced with the eternal sweet-versus-savory dilemma, I indulged in both: a Taylor ham, egg, and cheese sandwich and a short stack of blueberry pancakes. Leftovers are never a bad thing, after all.

The sandwich was fantastic. Initially nervous when they were out of Kaiser rolls, I opted for a hamburger bun—an excellent decision. This was no average bun; it was fresh and substantial. They layered the cheese perfectly, which to me is essential for a proper egg sandwich. It came with home fries sautéed with large slices of peppers and onions. I’m not usually a breakfast potato enthusiast, but these were delicious and clearly cooked to order, not scooped from a pre-made pile.

The pancakes were wonderfully fluffy. My only minor complaint was the Smuckers packaged syrup. I understand that syrup in individual containers rarely is real maple, but part of me wishes I didn’t have the confirmation of a sub-par offering.

Service was outstanding—friendly, attentive, with constant refills of actually good coffee (a diner rarity!). Bonus points to the server for kindly agreeing not to judge my dual breakfast order.

All around, I loved this place and hope to return soon. Long live the Jersey diner!

input:
im going to have to give this place one star for its horrible customer service:

i called in to ask about the 50% off for tulane students they were advertising, the woman assured me if i came with an id it would be half off and made an appointment for me, only once i got there did they tell me it's only on certain days, "it says it right on the sign," i was perturbed by the inconvenience and said so you're not going to honor it even though you just made an appointment with me and told me it would be 50% off, they said no flat out at first even though the error was blatantly on their side, after my nagging, she eventually called john jay himself and he told the woman that he would not honor what i was told even though i had been inconvenienced by someone in HIS staff because it might cause a 'domino effect,' i said how will there be a domino effect unless you continue to give people incorrect information, there will be no other 'dominoes' as long as you remember what day it is from now on... they began to treat me somewhat patronizingly as i explained that usually businesses make concessions when they are the one at fault, that the customer is supposed to always be right, yadda yadda yadda, i left pretty upset and with ~45 minutes of my life having been wasted - empty handed but for a lame excuse from someone who owns at least 3 businesses over 10 dollars...

i have not received a haircut from them so if you're one of those people who ONLY cares about the product and you think you'll get a good cut go right on ahead, but if you're like me (principled) and you don't like handing profits to people who care nothing about their customers this is a good place to skip next time you need a cut
Revise this with your best effort:
I must give this establishment a one-star review due to its abysmal customer service.

I called to inquire about the advertised 50% discount for Tulane students. The woman who answered assured me that bringing my ID would secure the half-off price and proceeded to schedule an appointment for me. However, upon my arrival, I was informed the discount was only valid on specific days. When I pointed out the inconvenience—having come in based on their employee’s explicit assurance—they refused to honor it, stating, “It says it right on the sign.”

Despite the error being entirely on their end, they initially denied my request outright. After persistent discussion, the staff member eventually called the owner, John Jay. He instructed her not to honor the discount I was promised, justifying his decision by claiming it might cause a “domino effect.” I countered that a domino effect would only occur if they continued providing incorrect information, and that preventing future issues simply required keeping track of the correct days.

Throughout this exchange, their tone became increasingly patronizing. I explained that businesses typically make concessions when they are at fault and that customer satisfaction should be a priority, but my reasoning was dismissed. I left frustrated, having wasted roughly 45 minutes and receiving nothing but a feeble excuse from an owner of multiple businesses—all over a $10 discount.

I did not receive a haircut here, so if you value only the end result and believe you’ll get a good cut, you may proceed. However, if you are principled and prefer not to support businesses that disregard their customers, I recommend taking your patronage elsewhere.

input:
My friend and I visited Tampa for a concert, and about ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport he realized that he had purchased tickets for the wrong day. We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life."

All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. 

I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restaurant. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellent food, drinks and service. I give this restaurant my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.

We lingered for hours, and the owner, Brian, came out to chat, comped us a drink, and let us sample new appetizers he was developing, all on the house. He made us feel genuinely welcome.

We returned for drinks before and after the concert. Even when packed, the service remained excellent, and the food and drinks held up perfectly. I give Bricks of Ybor my highest recommendation. It will be my first stop the next time I’m in Tampa.

Given the inattentive service, chaotic staffing, and slow kitchen, it is unlikely I will return.

input:
In short, the food was decently good, but completely overpriced.  The guacamole and my Mojito were probably the highlight of the meal. I had the peach pork medallions, which were nicely cooked, but lacked flavor. I tried the corn cakes with Barbacoa and that was pretty good.  

The atmosphere was inviting with a hip feel if that's what you're looking for.  What was really annoying was the parking situation. For a place with price points such as these and limited parking spaces, a valet service should be provided either at a cost or complimentary.  Don't even try and park in the back of the building, it's tight and dangerous even getting there and back.  I ended up parking three blocks away and broke a sweat walking in the dead of summer to the front entrance.
Revise this with your best effort:
The meal was decent but overpriced. Highlights included the fresh guacamole and a well-made Mojito. My main, the peach pork medallions, was cooked nicely yet underseasoned, while the corn cakes with Barbacoa were a tastier choice.

The atmosphere itself is inviting and stylish. The major drawback was the parking. For a restaurant at this price point with such limited spaces, a valet service—whether complimentary or paid—is a reasonable expectation. The rear lot is dangerously tight and difficult to navigate. I ultimately parked three blocks away and arrived flustered after a sweltering summer walk.
