input:
This was a tough one!   On the merits of the wine, fairly average... I understand that the winery has more than one lable and other label is their premium wines.  I look forward to when that is available (I went two weeks ago so maybe it already is)     Location..   what's not to like?  On the pier!  A wonderful outdoor patio,  couldn't have a nicer setting to enjoy your tasting....   The staff were super, super nice,  I would give them an A+!  

So why only three stars?  It is because of the wine club!  Very expensive for the quality of the wines and stingy as HELL with the benefits to the members..   Most wine clubs will give you a free tasting every time you come in (after all, we are your best customers... we are the ones who buy your wine time and time again).  Some wineries will give their members a complimentary glass in leau of a tasting (Carr).   Most wineries allow you to bring guests which is how you get new wine club members.   This system works folks!  The way this wine club works is that you are given a very limited number of passes per quarter, five as I recall.   If I come with my wife once a month we wouldn't even be covered... let alone if we bring a guest!   

So go to this winery if you want to enjoy a tasting in one of the most beautiful settings on earth.   But avoid the wine club!  For that you can pretty much go to any of the other wine tasting rooms on the Urban wine trail.
Revise this with your best effort:
This was a challenging review to write! Based purely on the wine, the experience was fairly average. I understand the winery has another label for its premium wines, and I look forward to trying those when available (I visited two weeks ago, so perhaps they are now).

The location, however, is exceptional—right on the pier! The wonderful outdoor patio provides a stunning setting for a tasting, which couldn’t be nicer. The staff were also superb, earning a solid A+ for their warmth and service.

So, why only three stars? The reason is the wine club. It’s very expensive for the quality offered and surprisingly stingy with member benefits. Most clubs provide a complimentary tasting for members each visit—after all, we are their best, repeat customers. Some, like Carr Winery, even offer a complimentary glass instead. Additionally, many wineries allow members to bring guests, which is a proven way to attract new members.

This winery’s system, by contrast, provides a very limited number of passes per quarter (five, as I recall). If my wife and I visit just once a month, we wouldn’t be fully covered, let alone if we brought a guest!

My advice? Visit this winery to enjoy a tasting in one of the most beautiful settings around. But I’d recommend avoiding the wine club. For that, you can find better value and perks at almost any other tasting room on the Urban Wine Trail.

They discovered the timing chain needed to be replaced, a chain that lasts the life of the car unless you don't change the oil or have low oil pressure the tensioner can lock and stretch the chain. Joe the service associate that took the car in specifically said I told the insurance company as little as possible and told them he couldn't tell if it was from the oil and there was no way to tell. And on top of that, was extremely rude and unprofessional to my wife bringing her to tears the way he spoke to her. My wife and I just bought a house in the area, only 26 years old and you lost a life long customer. Over the past year we spent about $7000 in repairs here, and Joe went out of his way to be unhelpful and leave us in a terrible spot. I brought it to another mechanic who was able to help us prove more it was from the oil and do what Joe told us and the insurance company they could not do. So on top of losing a service customer, I'm on the market for a new car and can tell you for sure where I will not be getting it.
Revise this with your best effort:

Their insurance company agreed to cover repairs if done at a dealership, and as frequent customers, we naturally brought the vehicle to you.

Worse, he was profoundly rude and unprofessional to my wife, speaking to her in a manner that brought her to tears.

input:

input:
The best soon-dubu in the city!  This place is tucked away and once you walk in, it's like you've stepped into a Korean home.  Very welcoming, warm and inviting.

It's very vegetarian friendly!  The soft tofu is stewed and put into the dol sot pots which each and every stew feels like it's custom made for you. 

You can select from beef, seafood or mixed meats (seafood & beef), mushroom, and just plain.  They can adjust the spice as needed too.  I always get the extra hot with the hot temperature, can't beat it.  The rice also comes in a dol-sot which is great if you leave it in for a while, it burns the rice into a nice crispy shell.  DROOL.

Just thinking about this place makes my mouth salivate!  

If you're not into tofu, they also offer korean bbq meats (cooked in the back), with other soup/stew items.

Love this place!!!
Revise this with your best effort:
The finest soon-dubu in the city! Tucked away, the moment you enter feels like stepping into a welcoming Korean home—warm and inviting.

It’s wonderfully vegetarian-friendly. The soft tofu is stewed and served in sizzling *dol sot* pots, each feeling custom-made.

You can choose from beef, seafood, mixed (seafood and beef), mushroom, or plain. They’ll adjust the spice level, too. I always order extra hot—nothing beats it. The rice also comes in a stone bowl; left to sit, it forms a perfect crispy shell. Just thinking about it makes my mouth water.

If tofu isn’t your preference, they also offer Korean BBQ meats (cooked in the kitchen) alongside other soups and stews.

An absolute favorite!

input:

Don't forget to grab a really great snack too while you're there- they have amazing chocolate bars, an incredible drink case, tons of chip varieties and those addictive hi-chew candies in every flavor.

I know i'll be back here, who doesn't like fast / delicious / attentive service?

From the moment you enter, you’re warmly welcomed by the kind woman at the counter. If you’re a regular—visiting more than once a week—she’ll likely remember your name. My own visits are a bit too sporadic for that, but the friendly atmosphere is always consistent.

My latest favorite is the vegetarian breakfast sandwich, available all day. I love the version with veggie sausage and Havarti on an everything bagel—I could honestly go for one right now. I’ve also tried the veggie club, while my partner has enjoyed the chicken cheesesteak hoagie and the chicken salad on a croissant. Every item tastes wonderfully fresh, and the prices are excellent (my preferred bagel sandwich is just $2.09–$2.99—even less than Wawa!). The deli staff are incredibly helpful, offering menus and making thoughtful suggestions or adjustments to suit your preferences.

Be sure to pick up a snack before you leave. They stock fantastic chocolate bars, an impressive drink cooler, a wide array of chips, and those irresistible Hi-Chew candies in every flavor.

I’ll definitely be returning. Who wouldn’t appreciate service that’s quick, delicious, and genuinely attentive?

input: Nice little bar located at the very far end of Terminal E and Tampa International. The airport recently added several new restaurants with a "local vibe" and this is one of them. There isn't a ton of seating but it also isn't close to the TSA area so it's a bit hidden. Hey have TVs if you wanna catch a game while you wait for your flight. Food is very reasonably price for the portion size. Appetizers run from $5-$10 and majority of sandwiches are $12. I didn't order any food but it looked amazing! Drinks are tasty and Prices are not terrible. Think 22oz Jai Alai for $8.50. You cannot take alcoholic beverages into the terminal (Columbia does this I think). I had a Manhattan for $11 and it was very tasty. Staff is attentive and friendly. I know my new spot when I'm waiting on a Delta flight!
Revise this with your best effort:
Tucked away at the far end of Terminal E in Tampa International, this nice little bar is part of the airport's newer "local vibe" additions. Its somewhat hidden location, away from the main TSA area, means it’s rarely crowded despite limited seating. Multiple TVs make it a good spot to catch a game before your flight.

The food looks amazing, with reasonably priced portions—appetizers range from $5-$10, and most sandwiches are around $12. Drink prices are fair, like a 22oz Jai Alai for $8.50 or a well-made Manhattan for $11. Note that you cannot take alcoholic beverages into the terminal. With its attentive, friendly staff, this has become my new go-to spot when waiting for a Delta flight.

My nearest exit was blocked, forcing a longer walk out.

If deep cleaning was necessary, the store should have closed temporarily. The entire ordeal wasted more time than a trip to Wegmans would have taken. From now on, that’s where I’ll shop.

input:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

I rarely write reviews, but this honestly was one of the worst group dining experiences I've ever had. It was objectively a horrible experience, even without comparing it to the hype it receives, and ruined what was supposed to be a nice birthday dinner celebration. 

We had a group of 8 that had a reservation made well in advance. Short wait, but not too bad. Keep in mind, it seemed like a normal Friday night, but weren't super busy or at-capacity.

It was a birthday dinner, so I told the hostesses that it was her birthday, and asked if they could bring out something for her at the end of the meal, which was acknowledged. Pretty standard stuff, whether at a Applebee's or the French Laundry. We were sat at a booth right next to the Maitre D' stand, and next to all the wait staff's home base, so pretty much no excuse for not getting any attention. 

After getting us waters, it took them a LONG time to even come by and acknowledge us. After ordering wine, it took them another good 15-20 minutes to even bring us our wine, and no one even checked in on us! (hint: if you're running a restaurant, wine is your profit center and doesn't take any work other than taking a bottle off a shelf and opening it. bring it out ASAP...). 

After ordering food, it was more of the same...a long wait for food to start coming out and no one checking in on us AT ALL. We drank the bottles we ordered and had to get up and flag someone down to get another wine order. A couple of us even got up during the meal to remind them to bring out something for birthday girl at the end of the meal. 

Once our meal was done and taken away, we were given dessert menus and the server disappeared for 10-15 minutes... AGAIN. After coming back, he asked what dessert we wanted, so we ordered some coffees... and waited... and waited. Eventually we got up and asked him what was going on and if they were going to bring anything out like we asked multiple times. 

They finally brought out a couple of cookies with a candle...

In summary, the food was pretty hit or miss, pretty mediocre for this price point. Whipped feta, like other reviews have said, was amazing, and the Braised Lamb was really good. But the Sirloin was chewy and bland and the Grilled Caesar tasted like a soggy, luke-warm, wilted mess (two orders were left untouched by a group of 8). Atmosphere was nice and trendy. But the service, which is a huge reason to spend your hard-earned $ at a restaurant, was absolutely horrendous. 

I really love going to cool, popular restaurants and having a great time, and I hate writing such a negative review, but I had to share my experience, especially for a restaurant that is getting an awful lot of (undeserved) hype.
Revise this with your best effort:
-------- DINNER REVIEW ----------

I seldom write reviews, but this stands as one of my worst group dining experiences. Objectively horrible, it ruined a planned birthday celebration, independent of the restaurant’s considerable hype.

Our party of eight had a reservation made well in advance. We waited briefly to be seated—a normal Friday night, but the restaurant was not at capacity.

Upon arrival, I informed the hostesses it was a birthday dinner and requested a small acknowledgment at the meal’s end—a standard practice anywhere. We were seated at a booth adjacent to the Maître D' stand and the main service station, placing us at the epicenter of staff activity. There was no conceivable excuse for inattention.

After delivering water, our table was ignored for a long interval. We ordered wine, then waited 15-20 minutes merely for its arrival, with no check-in in between. (A note: wine is a primary profit driver; delivering it promptly is basic.) The pattern persisted after ordering food. Courses arrived slowly, and we were utterly neglected. We finished our bottles and had to physically flag down a staff member to order more. During the meal, several of us separately reminded servers about the birthday gesture.

When dinner was cleared, dessert menus appeared, and our server vanished for another 10-15 minutes. Upon his return, we ordered coffee and dessert, then resumed waiting. Eventually, we rose to inquire about both the order and the forgotten birthday request. The acknowledgment, when it finally came, was a couple of cookies with a candle.

Summarily, the food was inconsistent and mediocre for the price. As other reviews note, the whipped feta was excellent, and the braised lamb was very good. However, the sirloin was chewy and bland, and the grilled Caesar salad arrived as a soggy, lukewarm, wilted mess—two orders went completely untouched by our group of eight. The atmosphere is indeed trendy and appealing. But service, a fundamental reason to spend hard-earned money dining out, was absolutely horrendous.

I take no pleasure in such a negative account. I cherish visiting popular, well-regarded spots. However, given the substantial (and, in my experience, undeserved) hype this restaurant commands, I felt compelled to share this candid assessment.

input:

In Tampa, the International Plaza Mall has this temporary store from Thanksgiving to Easter. They located very close to H&M clothing store. You can have samples before you buy it. input:
Second stop for Center City Restaurant Week:  R2L, dinner for $35 each. 

On the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place is a very fancy-cool restaurant/lounge where you can get a bird's eye view of the city! Group of us went to dinner here together after a day of meetings. Didn't get one of the tables facing the windows, but still had great views of the sunset and city by night. Again, multiple choices for the three courses, but I chose to start with the crisp peas/ham/garlic risotto [balls]. Main course was the Butcher's Filet (braised short rib + Steuben bean chili, potato/farm veg slaw and basil), which was quite heavy since there was also meat in the chili as well. The dazzling dessert to finish it off was the milk chocolate + hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel and coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. A bottle of wine for the table as well. Food was great, waiter was awesome (making sure to warn me that the risotto came in ball form rather than a bowl, for instance), very classy experience.
Revise this with your best effort:
Our second stop for Center City Restaurant Week was R2L, where we enjoyed the $35 dinner menu. Perched on the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place, this sophisticated restaurant and lounge offers a breathtaking bird’s-eye view of the city. Our group headed there for dinner after a day of meetings. Although we didn’t secure a window table, we still enjoyed stunning vistas of the sunset and the glittering skyline by night.

The prix-fixe menu offered multiple choices for each of the three courses. I began with crisp pea, ham, and garlic risotto balls. For the main course, I selected the Butcher’s Filet—a braised short rib served with Steuben bean chili (which contained additional meat), a potato and farm vegetable slaw, and basil. It was a decidedly hearty dish. The meal culminated in a dazzling dessert: milk chocolate and hazelnut pudding accompanied by salted caramel, a side of coffee for melting the chocolate, and candied almonds.

We shared a bottle of wine, and the entire experience was exceptional. The food was excellent, and our waiter was attentive and thoughtful—even noting that the risotto would arrive as balls, not in a bowl. It was a truly classy evening.

input:
I moved from Chicago to Philadelphia over a year ago.  Everybody here raves about the restaurants, but I have yet to find many that deserve five stars, or even four.  This is the best restaurant I have eaten in in Philadelphia.  

Tahini and bread  arrived at the table, and I thought, hum, plain but I'm hungry.  They must put crack in that Tahini.  I wanted to lap it out of the bowl like an uncouth dog.  The bread is excellent too.

I love a menu with many organic meat choices.  How often can you order an organic beef shishkabob?  It was superb.  The meat done perfectly, the onions nearly caramelized but not quite so they still had some substantive crunch.  The purslane salad tasted like I was eating a plant in the middle of a garden.  It is not often that I dream about a salad but I do dream about this one

My husband had a chicken dish with black eyed peas and green peas and fantastic rice.  I won't begin to describe the flavoring; it is beyond my culinary vocabulary.  We asked what spices they use, and in addition to traditional zatar, they use their own blend of spices.  I don't even need to know what is in it just so long as we can keep coming back and ordering it again and again.

I was so full but ate dessert none the less, which I usually don't do.  But when a diner is this good, I had a feeling the desserts would be too and I just needed to find out.  Pistachio creme brulee.  It could have come out over the top, but no indeed.  It was pure pistachio heaven in s super light yet rich custard.  Heaven. Heaven.

Our service was superb.  The squeezed us into a last minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to get through our dinner in an hour and 15 minutes in order to accommodate a reservation made prior to us.  Given the time constraints they never made us feel rushed and timed the meal perfectly.  Then my husband left to go to the restroom, the waiter picked up his napkin and refolded it nicely on the table.  Do I care about the napkin placement in the middle of a meal?  Not really, but it is a sign that the waitstaff is incredibly attentive and extremely well trained.  

My eating out plan for Philly might just be to skip eating most everywhere most of the time so I can frequent this expensive, though appropriately priced restaurant.  Kudos to the chef.
Revise this with your best effort:
After more than a year of calling Philadelphia home, I’ve listened to endless praise for the city’s dining scene, yet I’ve found few establishments that truly earn a four- or five-star rating in my book. This restaurant is the exception. It is, without reservation, the best I have experienced here.

The meal began simply with tahini and bread. My initial thought was, “Plain, but I’m hungry.” That notion vanished with the first taste. They must put crack in that tahini—I had to restrain myself from lapping it directly from the bowl like an uncouth dog. The accompanying bread was equally excellent.

I was immediately drawn to a menu featuring numerous organic meat options. How often does one find an organic beef shishkabob? It was superb: the meat cooked to perfect tenderness, the onions nearly caramelized yet retaining a substantive crunch. The purslane salad tasted as if I were eating a plant freshly plucked from a garden. I rarely dream of salads, but I dream of this one.

My husband ordered a chicken dish with black-eyed peas, green peas, and fantastic rice. The flavor profile was so complex it defies my culinary vocabulary. When we inquired about the spices, we learned they use traditional za’atar alongside a proprietary house blend. I don’t need to know what’s in it; I only need to know we can return to order it again and again.

Despite being full, I ventured into dessert—a rarity for me. When a kitchen is this skilled, intuition demands investigation. The pistachio crème brûlée could have been over-the-top, but it was instead a revelation: pure pistachio heaven in a super light, yet profoundly rich custard. Heaven. Simply heaven.

Service matched the quality of the food. They accommodated a last-minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to conclude within an hour and fifteen minutes. Despite this constraint, they never made us feel rushed, pacing the meal impeccably. At one point, my husband left for the restroom, and the waiter promptly retrieved his fallen napkin, refolding it neatly on the table. Do I care about napkin placement mid-meal? Not really. But it signals an incredibly attentive and well-trained staff.

My new Philadelphia dining strategy may be to forgo meals elsewhere, saving both appetite and budget for this restaurant. It is expensive, yet every penny feels justified. Kudos to the chef.

input:
Uhhhhh.... Not sure how to quantify or qualify my experience here. Let's start with back story: 

My sister was visiting for the weekend, so I wanted to show her a solid night on the town that lasted till the wee hours of the morning. We started on Frenchmen, but for whatever reason it was dead. 
Deciding to adventure Uptown we proceeded on a respectable bar crawl, including Delachaise, Columns, and St. Joes, however, at 3 AM the usual Uptown culprits start to raise their heads. A summary of the following dialogue:

Friends "Let's go to FMs" 
Me: "No, too much broken glass"
Friends: "Let's go to Snake and Jake's"
Me: "Eh...."
Friends: "Brothers 3?"
Me: "I'm afraid I'll hit my head on the ceiling"
Friends: "The Saint!!"
Me: "I suppose I haven't been there before, I'm curious."

After entering the Saint the look on my sisters face was priceless, akin to a deer in headlights look. I kept my countenance, and we ordered a round. Things proceeded as expected ... unwanted dance grinding advances, check! uber drunk guy talking your ear off, check! Big Buck Hunter, CHECK!!! Overall I'm glad I moderately traumatized my sister and sated my curiosity in the same night. 

Helpful hint: They have outdoor seating, surprisingly, which is very good to escape the smoke
Revise this with your best effort:
My sister was visiting for the weekend, and I wanted to give her a proper, late-night tour of the city. We began on Frenchmen Street, but it was unexpectedly quiet. Seeking more energy, we ventured Uptown for a respectable bar crawl, hitting spots like Delachaise, Columns, and St. Joe’s. By 3 a.m., however, the typical late-night options emerged, leading to a familiar debate among friends.

The suggestions flew: "Let’s go to F&M’s." I declined, citing too much broken glass. "Snake and Jake’s?" I was hesitant. "Brothers 3?" I worried I’d hit my head on the low ceiling. Then someone said, "The Saint!" Having never been, my curiosity won out.

Upon entering, my sister’s deer-in-headlights expression was priceless. I maintained my composure as we ordered a round. The scene unfolded exactly as one might predict: unwanted dance-floor advances, an overly chatty drunk, and a round of Big Buck Hunter. In the end, I managed to both mildly traumatize my sister and satisfy my own curiosity in a single night.

A helpful tip: they have outdoor seating, which provides a surprisingly good escape from the indoor smoke.

input:
I love trying fresh seafood on piers, wharfs and seaside markets. Most of the time, it is a disappointing experience but this place is not. The food is legitimately fresh and prepared well. The gorgeous view is just a cherry on top of nature's beautiful sundae. I have been here before but ordered the "wrong" thing (cioppino). That wasn't very good when I had it a couple of years ago here. 

We came for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday. Even at 4pm,  there was a wait! We waited about 25 minutes and got a table outdoor. While it wasn't ideal that we sat right in the sun with no shelter other than our sunscreen and sunglasses, the view was worth it. 

We got the local crab special which was a steamed 3-lb. crab served with a salad and soup for $26. I thought this was quite the steal because the crab was huge, delicious and meaty. The garden salad was fresh as simple as it was. The lobster bisque we got was pretty good. (The other options were Caesar salad and clam chowder). They topped off the crab with a couple of onion rings and cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Yum!

We also got the fried platter of shrimp, oysters, calamari and scallops for $12.95. It came with cole slaw, onion rings, tartar sauce and cocktail sauce. As greasy of a meal as this made, it was one of the better fried platters I've had anywhere. The seafood was just really fresh including the sometimes-feared fried oyster. :)

The ice in our iced teas melted away in the sun. Our waitress was so cool and brought us lots of extra ice and an extra iced tea in case we needed it (we did because it was hot out!). She was just friendly and good at her job - five stars for her!

By the time we left at about 6, there were so many people waiting. Make sure you sign up for a seat on the clipboard right when you get there. The restaurant is the last one at the very end of the pier. Parking on the pier is free for 90 minutes but it looks like a drive that will upset tires. I parked in the large lot south of the pier and walked 15 minutes up and onto the pier. It was free on a Monday late afternoon.
Revise this with your best effort:
I adore sampling fresh seafood at piers, wharves, and coastal markets, though the experience is often a letdown. This place, however, is a glorious exception. The food is authentically fresh and skillfully prepared, and the stunning ocean vista is merely the cherry on top of nature’s beautiful sundae. I had visited before but ordered the “wrong” item—the cioppino—which was underwhelming a couple of years ago.

We arrived for a late lunch or early dinner on a Monday. Even at 4 p.m., there was a wait! After about 25 minutes, we were seated outdoors. While our table was directly in the sun with no shade beyond sunscreen and sunglasses, the panoramic view made it worthwhile.

We chose the local crab special: a steamed three-pound crab served with a salad and soup for $26. This felt like a steal—the crab was enormous, delicious, and packed with meat. The garden salad was fresh in its simplicity. We opted for the lobster bisque, which was quite good (the alternatives were Caesar salad or clam chowder). The crab was garnished with a few onion rings and accompanied by cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Yum!

We also shared the fried platter ($12.95), featuring shrimp, oysters, calamari, and scallops. It came with coleslaw, onion rings, tartar sauce, and cocktail sauce. Though it made for a greasy meal, it was one of the finest fried seafood assortments I’ve had anywhere. Every component was remarkably fresh, even the sometimes-intimidating fried oyster. :)

The ice in our iced teas melted swiftly in the heat. Our waitress was wonderfully attentive, bringing us ample extra ice and even a supplemental iced tea—which we needed! She was genuinely friendly and efficient, earning a solid five stars.

By our departure around 6 p.m., the crowd had grown considerably. Be sure to add your name to the clipboard waitlist immediately upon arrival. The restaurant is the very last one at the pier’s end. Pier parking is free for 90 minutes, but the rugged surface seems tough on tires. I parked in the large lot south of the pier and enjoyed a 15-minute stroll up and onto the pier—free on a Monday late afternoon.

*(Approximately 405 words)*

input:

input:
I stayed at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday.

Arrival: I already read plenty of reviews about no signs marking the location therefore, I looked for Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi business complex. I went inside to find a guard at a desk that said we have been contracted to hand guests their keys and room number and nothing more. He advised me there was a phone that was on the wall that I could make a call to someone if I needed to. He also stated that the very few parking spots in front were free* only on the weekend.

The Room: This wasn't a room, this was an apartment and I absolutely loved it. It was very spacious and had everything I sought* after for that weekend, such as: fully stocked kitchen, a desk, lots of space, king bed, huge table, nice living room, lots of closets. My only complaint is that I could not open any windows for fresh air...they are nailed/screwed shut. There was also a small welcome bag w cookies and water and papers letting you know where all the food delivery locations and numbers.
There wasn't maid service knocking loudly or trying to barge in early in the morning. This place is more of a long term setting and I'm sure the maids come around during the week Monday-Friday if you desire. I was only here for 3 days and I was fine with that. I went shopping at Shoprite and filled my fridge with water and breakfast to cook.

Overall: This place is awesome, I had a huge living room to entertain my guests when they visited, and a nice desk to study my Anatomy notes. I forgot to mention how quiet** this place is. I loved it. I felt as if no one was there except me. Very quiet* which worked for me on Sunday bc I had lots of studying to do and two TV's to watch The Walking Dead on. Lol!  I would most definitely stay here again. Very spacious and updated. Loved it!
Revise this with your best effort:
I stayed at the Orange Street location from Friday to Monday.

**Arrival:** Having read numerous reviews about the lack of signage, I looked for the nearby Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi-business complex and went inside. A guard at the desk informed me they were only contracted to distribute keys and room numbers. For any questions, he pointed to a wall phone to call someone. He also noted the few front parking spots were complimentary only on weekends.

**The Room:** This was not merely a room, but a full apartment, and I absolutely loved it. It was incredibly spacious and had everything I needed: a fully stocked kitchen, a desk, a king bed, a large dining table, a comfortable living room, and ample closet space. My sole complaint was that none of the windows could be opened for fresh air, as they were sealed shut. A small welcome bag contained cookies, water, and information with local food delivery options. The absence of daily maid service was a plus—no loud knocks or early disturbances. This is clearly set up for longer-term stays, with cleaning likely available on weekdays. For my three-day stay, it was perfect. I shopped at Shoprite and stocked the fridge for breakfast.

**Overall:** This place is awesome. The huge living room was ideal for entertaining visiting guests, and the desk provided an excellent space to study anatomy. input: I had the worst experience of my life and it's not over yet.  I made a mistake in purchasing a vehicle that is out of my budget on a Friday afternoon. He stated he would speak with his manager and call me back.  At 3:30 after no return call, I called him again, no answer. I left a voicemail and still no call at closing time.  Monday morning I arrived at the dealership as they were opening.  I asked Stephen, the salesman what they determined.  He instructed me to have a seat and he would talk to his management team.  One hour + later, I was called into a cubicle and told my loan had been funded and the title had been changed.  Therefore, I would have to sell the car back to the dealership as a used car.  I would lose a lot of money in doing this.  This morning, Bill head of finance advised that the bank had questions about funding the loan.  I received a call from the bank stating the loan had NOT been funded and they would be unable to okay the loan.  I have left numerous messages with the dealership and have yet to receive a callback.  I contacted an attorney and per his review I again called the dealership and asked for a time to return the vehicle and take back my trade.  Still no response!  These people will lie to your face, avoid this dealership!!

My recent experience stands as the most distressing of my life, and it remains unresolved. It began when I made the serious error of purchasing a vehicle beyond my means on a Friday afternoon. By Sunday, after a careful budget review, I realized I could not afford it.

I called the salesman at 11:30 a.m. to explain my predicament. He said he would consult his manager and call me back. By 3:30 p.m., with no word, I called again—no answer. I left a voicemail, but received no callback by closing time.

On Monday morning, I arrived as the dealership opened. I asked Stephen, the salesman, for their decision. He told me to have a seat while he spoke with management. I have left numerous messages with the dealership, yet I have received no callback. After consulting an attorney, I called again, requesting a time to return the vehicle and reclaim my trade-in. Still, there has been no response.

This dealership will lie to your face. I urge everyone to avoid it entirely.

input:
I have been a patron of Desi Village in West Philly for years.  After moving the suburbs, we saw the KOP Desi Village and finally tried it.  We were skeptical having also tried Mood Cafe (owned by the W.Philly folks), and it wasn't as good. But the KOP location is actually very comparable to the West Philly location.  

There is no ambiance or atmosphere here.  The strip mall where it's located is pretty depressing.  Desi Village may be the only active store in it.  And its decor is tired and old.  It is a big space and it appears they do a big lunch buffet but I'm curious if it's ever full.  So don't go for the ambiance.

But the food is good.  We ordered some Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani.  All of it was really good.  Perfectly seasoned, not too oily, and appropriately spicy.  I have a nut allergy and made them aware of that and they did not screw it up (most Indian restaurants do).  So we'll definitely be back.  It would be great if they moved into nicer digs but the food is what is most important.
Revise this with your best effort:
I have been a loyal customer of Desi Village in West Philly for years. After moving to the suburbs, we noticed the King of Prussia location and decided to give it a try. We were skeptical, having also tried Mood Cafe—another venture from the West Philly owners—which didn’t measure up. However, the KOP Desi Village is actually very comparable to the original.

Do not come here for ambiance. The strip mall is bleak, with Desi Village seemingly its only active tenant. Inside, the decor is dated and worn. It’s a large space that appears geared for a lunch buffet, though I wonder if it ever fills up.

But the food is excellent. We ordered keema naan, samosas, saag paneer, and lamb biryani. Everything was perfectly seasoned, not overly oily, and had just the right level of spice. As someone with a nut allergy, I informed the staff and they handled it flawlessly—a rare success in my experience with Indian restaurants.

We will definitely return. While a nicer setting would be welcome, the quality of the food is what truly matters.

input:
What an AMAZING occurrence that we ended up here after another barbecue place ran out of food!

So yeah, we started out at another spot and they were out of food when we got there. I decided to get the one-meat plate with "wet" pulled pork, grits and potato salad, I also got a medium mac and cheese, because I can. My boyfriend got the two-meat plate with brisket and pulled chicken with potato salad and fries. The food blew us both away! It was delicious from beginning to end. I will definitely return to LA Smokehouse and I'll be adding it to my "BBQ Favorites" list for future reference.

input:
After today's lunch, Iris has moved to the top of my New Orleans favorites lists--no small feat in a city where restaurants are numerous and culinary competition is fierce. Iris excels in every area: food, drinks, service, atmosphere, location, music and overall graciousness. I made the reservation for 10-15 people, not knowing exactly how many in my party would show up. Iris pulled out all the stops to make sure everyone had comfortable seating and even prepared an overflow table for us. At no time did we feel jostled or rushed, which is a common fine dining concern. 

The layout of the restaurant allowed diners to move freely to and from the table and to exchange seats as needed. The music selection was fun and unique, ranging from the Magnetic Fields to Johnny Cash. It was also quiet enough to be enjoyed while allowing conversation to flow unimpeded. Our waiter had excellent timing and anticipated our every need. 

Though they don't have a full drink menu for lunch (I hear they have an amazing mixologist for the dinner hour) they do offer a selection of martinis and wines. One of the guests has accounts with several high-end bars in the Quarter, and the drink list passed his muster. Our table settled for Chardonnays, Perseco and chilled shots of Chartreuse, though I hear they have several types of absinthe as well. 

Our group began with slices of warm, heavenly bread that Iris bakes in house. We continued with an assortment of salads--I had the Hollygrove arugula with warm goat cheese, niçoise olives and balsamic vinaigrette. It was fresh perfection. A few of us opted for the mussels, which I heard were delicious. For my main course, I had a wonderful drum with onions prepared in a tangy soy reduction, which was an elegant complement for the fish. I also heard rave reviews about the gnocci and chicken. 

All the entrees were creatively arranged and selected, and at no point did I feel overwhelmed or that any fuss or pretense had gone into the food. I also appreciated that the portions were European-sized (it always makes me laugh when other Americans list too-small portion size as a complaint even when the food is well-prepared!). Iris prepares a lot of their basic ingredients in-house, and I appreciate that the kitchen makes a point of incorporating gulf fish and produce purchased from local, farmer-friendly markets. 

We settled on the prix fixe menu, which was $20 a person for appetizer, main course and the dessert of the day (the best strawberry sorbet I have had yet). With the added drinks and tip it came out to under $35 a person, which is an excellent price for such a delicious white-linen lunch. No matter the size of my group, I will definitely be returning!

The staff and manager really know customer service.  Look forward to returning soon!

input:
Another great annual festival Edmonton has to offer.

The Fringe is over two weekends and the joining week full of performances. There's a variety of venues and plays to watch, street performers and musicians. There's a schedule online to find show times, buy tickets and learn more about the artists. 

Half of 104th closes down to add space for a variety of food vendors and artisan vendors (art, jewelry, clothing, etc.).

Good tip: there's a gourmet mini donut truck off behind the farmers market a bit tucked away. Amazing!

It's nice to take an hour or two before or after a show to walk around and casually stumble on other street performances. Or even go without seeing a play just to snack and shop at the vendors.

The location is absolutely fabulous.
Revise this with your best effort:
Edmonton offers another outstanding annual festival: the Fringe. Spanning two weekends and the week in between, it’s packed with performances. You’ll find a diverse array of plays across multiple venues, plus street musicians and performers. Check the online schedule for showtimes, tickets, and artist details.

Half of 104th Street closes to make room for numerous food and artisan vendors, selling everything from art and jewelry to clothing. A pro tip: seek out the gourmet mini-donut truck tucked behind the farmers’ market—it’s amazing!

The location is fabulous. You can easily spend an hour or two before or after a show wandering, casually discovering street performances. Many visit just to snack and shop, without even seeing a play.

input:
A great spot to take out-of-town guests. I take all my Chicago friends here and they fall in love. The burgers are incredible and the boozy shakes are like no other. The first time I had horchata shake I honestly had dreams about it for like a week. It's also super centrally located, a quick walk from Wash Ave and other downtown attractions. Great vibe, although I always prefer to get a table upstairs than sit at the community tables on the ground floor.

The burger selection is really, really great. You can pretty much get whatever your heart desires. I've had mac n cheese patties on my burger, you can get a bison burger, turkey burger, literally anything. I have tried a ton and have never been let down by the flavor combinations. The waiters are always super honest, in a good way. If you ask them what's better, X or Y, they're not going to jerk you around and say they're equally good. They'll give you their honest opinion. LOVE that. 

Another unique aspect about Bailey's Range is that they have a burger showdown (can't remember their technical term for it) where last week's featured burger goes up against a new burger recipe. It's a cool call-out that you don't see at a lot of other restaurants. 

The only reason I gave it a 4/5 star instead of 5/5 is because I've had a couple of instances (out of MANY visits, so it's really not alarming or anything) where I requested my burger medium or medium-rare and it turned out a little well done. I still ate it, but it wasn't really what I expected.
Revise this with your best effort:
Bailey’s Range is my go-to spot for out-of-town guests—I bring all my Chicago friends here, and they inevitably fall in love. The burgers are incredible, and the boozy shakes are in a league of their own. My first horchata shake was so memorable I dreamed about it for a week. The location is super convenient, just a short walk from Washington Avenue and other downtown attractions. I also love the vibe, though I always aim for a table upstairs rather than the ground-floor community seating.

The burger selection is outstanding. Whether you crave a mac and cheese-topped patty, a bison burger, or a turkey burger, they truly have something for every taste. I’ve tried countless combinations and have never been disappointed. The waitstaff deserve a special shoutout for their genuine honesty. Ask them to choose between two items, and they’ll give a straightforward, helpful opinion—no waffling.

Another unique feature is their weekly burger showdown (I forget their exact name for it), where last week’s featured burger competes against a new recipe. It’s a creative touch you don’t see many places.

I’m rating Bailey’s Range 4 out of 5 stars instead of 5 only because, on a couple of occasions over many visits, my requested medium or medium-rare burger arrived closer to well-done. It wasn’t enough to ruin the meal, but it did stray from what I expected. That small inconsistency aside, this place remains a favorite I wholeheartedly recommend.
